comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the temporal consistency of behavioral traits (C37-C45) to be well-supported. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical tests and significant correlations in Table 1 and Figure 1. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the personality consistency findings without raising methodological concerns.

Disagreement on evidence strength. OpenEval rates C35-C36 (Pareto front interpretation) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical validation for the trade-off claim. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the descriptive characterization without challenging the interpretation, suggesting implicit acceptance.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations rate C53-C54, C88-C89 as UNCERTAIN due to differential attrition confound. OpenEval notes the inability to distinguish real effects from selection bias. Peer reviewers acknowledge the authors' own caution about this finding being 'a result of post-selection.'

Agreement. Both find C64-C66 (experience vs. age effects) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the statistical support and interesting implications. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the developmental trajectory analysis after revisions addressed persistence concerns.

Agreement. Both find temporal patterns in behavioral traits (C46-C50, C83, C86) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes clear documentation in Tables 2-3 and Figure 2. Peer reviewers accept these patterns after revisions, with the anonymous reviewer stating the paper is 'much stronger.'

Agreement. Both find null results for indoor behavioral measures (C51-C52, C82) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical approach and clear reporting. Peer reviewers treat this as an important methodological insight rather than a weakness, accepting the finding without challenge.

Agreement with nuance. Both find C69, C100-C101 (lack of indoor-outdoor correlation) SUPPORTED. OpenEval questions whether 'limited translation' interpretation may be overstated, suggesting context-specificity as alternative. Peer reviewers explicitly value this as a major strength showing importance of natural habitat testing.

Agreement. Both find outdoor behavioral findings (C55-C58, C90) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes substantial differences with appropriate data collection but flags high variability and modest sample size. Peer reviewers strongly affirm the GPS tracking findings without methodological concerns.

Agreement. Both find C59-C63, C72 (experience trumps predisposition) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical approach but mentions modest sample size and context differences. Peer reviewers treat this as a key contribution showing primacy of early experience over innate factors.

Agreement. Both find main conclusions (C5-C6, C70-C71, C103) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes support from GPS and GLMM analyses but cautions about causal interpretation requiring no confounding. Peer reviewers strongly affirm the core finding that enrichment shapes behavior.

Agreement. Both find C75-C78 (novelty claims and literature context) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and justified novelty claim. Peer reviewers emphasize the unique contribution, with both editor and anonymous reviewer highlighting the study's novel approach to natural behavior.
